kings1.22.p1.b1.text: Then three years passed without war between Aram and Israel. However, in the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel,

kings1.22.p1.b2.text: “Do you not know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, but we have failed to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?”

kings1.22.p1.b3.text: “Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth-gilead?”

kings1.22.p1.b4.text: “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”

kings1.22.p2.b1.text: “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”

kings1.22.p2.b2.text: “Go up,” they replied, “and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

kings1.22.p2.b3.text: “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”

kings1.22.p2.b4.text: “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.”

kings1.22.p3.b1.text: Dressed in royal attire, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

kings1.22.p3.b2.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.’”

kings1.22.p3.b3.text: “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

kings1.22.p4.b1.text: “Behold now, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.”

kings1.22.p4.b2.text: “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.”

kings1.22.p4.b3.text: “Go up and triumph,” Micaiah replied, “for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”

kings1.22.p4.b4.text: “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?”

kings1.22.p5.b1.text: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd.

kings1.22.p5.b2.text: ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’

kings1.22.p5.b3.text: “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?”

kings1.22.p6.b1.text: “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left.

kings1.22.p6.b2.text: ‘Who will entice Ahab to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’

kings1.22.p6.b3.text: So you see, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”

kings1.22.p7.b1.text: “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He departed from me to speak with you?”

kings1.22.p7.b2.text: “You will soon see, on that day when you go and hide in an inner room.”

kings1.22.p7.b3.text: ‘Put this man in prison and feed him only bread and water until I return safely.’

kings1.22.p7.b4.text: “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.”

kings1.22.p8.b1.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

kings1.22.p8.b2.text: “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes.”

kings1.22.p8.b3.text: “Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel.”

kings1.22.p8.b4.text: “Surely this is the king of Israel!”

kings1.22.p9.b1.text: However, a certain man drew his bow without taking special aim, and he struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor.

kings1.22.p9.b2.text: “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am badly wounded!”

kings1.22.p9.b3.text: And the blood from his wound ran out onto the floor of the chariot, and that evening he died.

kings1.22.p9.b4.text: “Every man to his own city, and every man to his own land!”

kings1.22.p10.b1.text: So the king died and was brought to Samaria, where they buried him.

kings1.22.p10.b2.text: …the dogs licked up Ahab’s blood, according to the word that the LORD had spoken.

kings1.22.p10.b3.text: And Ahab rested with his fathers,

kings1.22.p10.b4.text: and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.

kings1.22.p11.b1.text: And Jehoshaphat walked in all the ways of his father Asa; he did not turn away from them, but did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. The high places, however, were not removed…

kings1.22.p11.b3.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of his father and mother…

kings1.22.p11.b4.text: Ahaziah served and worshiped Baal, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger…
